goldenPoints: Colles fracture: dorsal displacement with dinner-fork deformity; Smith is its reverse.
Posterior hip dislocation: limb flexed, adducted, internally rotated and shortened.
Radial nerve palsy after humeral shaft fracture gives wrist drop; axillary nerve palsy follows surgical neck fracture.
Giant cell tumour: soap-bubble epiphyseal lesion in a 20-40 year old.
Osteosarcoma makes Codman triangle; Ewing sarcoma is the most radiosensitive bone tumour.
High calcium with a normal alkaline phosphatase means myeloma, not Paget disease.
Painful arc of 60-120 degrees of abduction points to supraspinatus pathology.
Common peroneal nerve injury at the fibular neck causes foot drop.
Salter-Harris type II is the commonest growth-plate fracture.
Young adult with femoral neck fracture: urgent reduction and internal fixation.
intro: Orthopaedics carries 5 marks per paper, and the PYQs lean heavily on images: named fractures, dislocated hips, bone tumours and nerve injuries. The coaching rapid-revision material confirms the same emphasis — fractures and dislocations first, then tumours, metabolic bone disease and clinical signs. These notes organise the subject the way the exam asks it: recognise the picture, name the nerve, pick the classic association.

subject: Orthopaedics
tagline: FMGE Orthopaedics is picture recognition: fractures, dislocations, tumours and the nerve that goes with each

topics.askedAs: named fracture from deformity or image
topics.oneLiner: Dinner fork means Colles — dorsal displacement; its mirror image, volar displacement, is Smith.
points: Colles fracture: distal radius, dorsal displacement and angulation, dinner-fork deformity.
Smith fracture is reverse Colles — volar displacement of the distal fragment.
Scaphoid is the most fractured carpal bone; anatomical snuffbox tenderness after a fall.
Bennett fracture: intra-articular fracture of first metacarpal base with subluxation of the shaft.
Rolando fracture: comminuted Y- or T-shaped intra-articular fracture of first metacarpal base.
Clavicle fractures most commonly involve the middle third of the bone.
Salter-Harris type II is the commonest growth-plate fracture pattern in children.
Fracture of both tibia and fibula at the same level is a both-bone leg fracture, graded open by Gustilo-Anderson when the skin breaks.

head: Fracture
Site
Signature
rows: Proximal ulna fracture, radial head dislocation
Distal radius fracture, distal radioulnar disruption

topics.title: Named Fractures & Classic Deformities
topics.trap: Bennett and Rolando are both first-metacarpal-base fractures — Bennett is two-part with subluxation, Rolando is comminuted.

topics.askedAs: nerve injured for a given fracture site
topics.oneLiner: Surgical neck-axillary, shaft-radial, elbow-ulnar and median, fibular neck-peroneal.
points: Axillary nerve: fracture of surgical neck of humerus; loss of abduction, regimental-badge sensory loss.
Radial nerve in spiral groove: humeral shaft fracture causes wrist drop with preserved elbow extension.
Holstein-Lewis fracture: lower-third humeral shaft fracture with radial nerve injury.
Median nerve: supracondylar fracture in children; pointing-index sign when making a fist.
Ulnar nerve is the nerve most commonly affected in leprosy — claw hand and hypothenar wasting.
Common peroneal nerve at fibular neck: foot drop, loss of dorsiflexion and eversion, numb dorsum of foot.
Metacarpal fracture with hypothenar atrophy points to ulnar nerve injury at the wrist.
Brachial plexus upper trunk (C5-C6) injury after shoulder trauma gives Erb palsy — waiter-tip hand.
topics.title: Fracture Complications & Nerve Injuries
topics.trap: Wrist drop with a midshaft humerus fracture is radial nerve; loss of shoulder abduction is axillary — different fractures, different nerves.

topics.askedAs: limb position in hip dislocation vignettes
topics.oneLiner: Posterior dislocation: short, adducted, internally rotated. Anterior: abducted, externally rotated, apparently long.
points: Posterior hip dislocation is the commonest type — after dashboard injury in a seated passenger.
Posterior dislocation posture: limb flexed, adducted, internally rotated and shortened.
Anterior dislocation posture: limb flexed, abducted, externally rotated, with apparent lengthening.
Posterior dislocation risks sciatic nerve injury and avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
Dislocated hip is an emergency: reduce within 6 hours to protect the femoral head blood supply.
Femoral neck fracture in a young adult: urgent anatomical reduction and internal fixation to save the head.
Displaced femoral neck fracture in the elderly: hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement.
Garden classification grades femoral neck fractures by completeness and displacement.
topics.title: Hip Dislocations & Femoral Neck Fractures
topics.trap: A fractured neck of femur also shortens the limb, but it lies externally rotated — internal rotation means dislocation.

topics.askedAs: tumour diagnosis from age, site, X-ray phrase
topics.oneLiner: Match three things: patient age, bone region (epiphysis/metaphysis/diaphysis), and the X-ray catchphrase.
points: Giant cell tumour: 20-40 years, epiphysis, eccentric lytic soap-bubble lesion, distal femur or proximal tibia.
Osteosarcoma: adolescent metaphysis, Codman triangle, sunray spicules; tumour produces osteoid.
Ewing sarcoma: diaphysis of long bones in children, onion-peel periosteal reaction.
Ewing sarcoma is the most radiosensitive bone tumour.
Osteochondroma (exostosis): commonest benign bone tumour; painless bony lump near the knee in adolescents.
Enchondroma: lytic lesion of small bones of the hand, classically the proximal phalanx.
Osteoid osteoma: night pain relieved by aspirin, small radiolucent nidus on imaging.
Chondroblastoma affects the epiphysis of adolescents — the benign epiphyseal tumour.
topics.title: Bone Tumours by Age & Site
topics.trap: Codman triangle appears in osteosarcoma stems, but it is a periosteal reaction — it can also occur in infection and Ewing tumour.

topics.oneLiner: Paget pushes alkaline phosphatase sky-high; myeloma raises calcium and leaves ALP normal.
points: Multiple myeloma: raised calcium, normal alkaline phosphatase, punched-out lytic skull lesions.
Paget disease: very high alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium and phosphate.
Primary hyperparathyroidism: high calcium, low phosphate, raised PTH; subperiosteal resorption of phalanges.
Brown tumours and osteitis fibrosa cystica are skeletal features of hyperparathyroidism.
Rickets is defective mineralisation of growing bone; osteomalacia is the same defect in adults.
Osteoporosis: reduced bone mass with normal mineralisation; fragility fractures of hip, spine, wrist.
FRAX estimates 10-year probability of hip and major osteoporotic fracture; a history of falls is not an input.
Marfan syndrome is caused by mutation of the fibrillin-1 gene (FBN1).
topics.title: Metabolic Bone Diseases
topics.trap: High calcium plus high ALP suggests hyperparathyroidism or malignancy with bone reaction; high calcium with normal ALP is the myeloma pattern.

topics.oneLiner: Short morning stiffness with bony nodes is OA; the post-diarrhoea triad is reactive arthritis.
points: Osteoarthritis: morning stiffness under 30 minutes, Heberden nodes at DIP and Bouchard at PIP joints.
Osteoarthritis X-ray: joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts.
Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetric small-joint polyarthritis with prolonged morning stiffness.
Gout: hyperuricaemia; allopurinol is first-line urate-lowering therapy and inhibits xanthine oxidase.
Acute gout attack is treated with NSAIDs or colchicine — do not start allopurinol during the flare.
Reactive arthritis follows genitourinary or gut infection: arthritis, urethritis, conjunctivitis.
Psoriatic arthritis combines skin and nail lesions with joint disease.
topics.title: Arthritis Patterns
topics.trap: Heberden nodes are DIP and Bouchard are PIP — rheumatoid arthritis characteristically spares the DIP joint.

topics.askedAs: hip and elbow problems of childhood
topics.oneLiner: Limping obese teenager with a stiff hip is SCFE until proven otherwise.
points: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis: obese adolescent, restricted abduction and internal rotation of hip.
Perthes disease: avascular necrosis of the femoral head in a child of 4-8 years.
Supracondylar humerus fracture is the classic elbow fracture of a child falling on an outstretched hand.
In supracondylar fracture the brachial artery and median nerve are at risk; watch for a pink, pulseless hand.
Volkmann ischaemic contracture is the late result of missed compartment syndrome in the forearm.
Developmental dysplasia of the hip is screened with Ortolani and Barlow tests in newborns.
Clubfoot (CTEV) is a congenital deformity combining equinus, varus and forefoot adduction.
topics.title: Paediatric Orthopaedics
topics.trap: Knee pain in an adolescent may be referred from the hip — always examine the hip in SCFE and Perthes.

topics.askedAs: test or sign name from the description
topics.oneLiner: Step in the back is spondylolisthesis; a 60-120 degree painful arc is the supraspinatus.
points: Painful arc syndrome: supraspinatus tendinitis hurts between 60 and 120 degrees of shoulder abduction.
Trendelenburg test: pelvis drops on the opposite side when abductor mechanism (gluteus medius) fails.
Thomas test unmasks a fixed flexion deformity of the hip hidden by lumbar lordosis.
Spondylolisthesis: forward slip of one vertebra, felt as a palpable step in the back.
Terrible triad of the elbow: dislocation with radial head and coronoid process fractures.
TB hip progresses through stages; the arthritis stage shows true shortening of the limb.
True shortening means bone loss or displacement; apparent shortening comes from pelvic tilt or deformity.
topics.title: Clinical Tests & Signs
topics.trap: Trendelenburg sign is named for the side of the stance leg whose abductors fail — the pelvis sags on the swinging side.

topics.oneLiner: Housemaid knee is a bursa, not a joint — prepatellar bursitis from kneeling work.
points: Acute osteomyelitis in children usually affects the metaphysis; Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism.
Chronic osteomyelitis shows sequestrum (dead bone) within involucrum (new bone sheath).
Tuberculosis of the hip is a chronic destructive arthritis ending in true shortening and deformity.
Spinal TB (Pott spine) most often involves the thoracolumbar vertebrae and can form a psoas abscess.
Prepatellar bursitis (housemaid knee): soft fluctuant swelling in front of the patella in workers who kneel.
Empyema and septic arthritis need urgent drainage — pus inside a joint destroys cartilage fast.
Brodie abscess is a localised, subacute form of osteomyelitis with a sclerotic rim.
topics.title: Bone & Joint Infections
topics.trap: A fluctuant swelling in FRONT of the patella is bursitis; an effusion is inside the joint and restricts movement far more.
